title: Göbekli Tepe datable because it was buried
summary: Matt LaCroix tells of Göbekli Tepe datable because it was buried, about c. 9600 BC at Göbekli Tepe, Turkey, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: GOC teepe was dated the only reason they were able to date gockley teepe is because the site was believed to be buried

plain: On a show hosted by a podcaster named Jesse Michels, a researcher named Matt LaCroix talks about Göbekli Tepe, an ancient site of big carved stone pillars in Turkey, dated to around 9600 BC. He says the only reason anyone could put a date on it is that the site was believed to have been buried, which matters because it suggests other old stone sites that were never buried may be older than anyone can show.
